subject: Liability carve-outs for Order Form — gross negligence threshold
messages:
From: Julia Ramos <julia.ramos@acme.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form liability language (MSA ref: RDW-2025)

Hi Rishi —

Thanks for sending the Order Form draft. Our legal team flagged Section 7 (Limitation of Liability) and wants clarity on gross negligence / willful misconduct carve-outs. Specifically: if we accept the 1x fees cap in the Order Form, will Redwood accept an uncapped carve-out for fraud and willful misconduct, and a separate threshold for gross negligence tied to material breach (i.e., loss beyond the cap if proven as material and reckless conduct)?

We also have questions about consequential damages exclusions for regulated data leak scenarios. Can you loop in your contracts/legal so we can get a clean redline quickly?

Attachments: ACME_Redline_Request.pdf (summary)

Best,
Julia Ramos
Sr. Counsel, Acme Corp

Quick ask from our side: is Acme comfortable with a separate negotiated threshold for gross negligence (e.g., material breach + reckless standard) versus an open-ended carve-out for all negligence? That framing will help us draft a concise redline.

I’ll aim to have a draft redline back by EOD Tuesday.

From: laura.bennett@redwood.com

Date: Tue, 16 Sep 2025 08:34:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order Form liability language (MSA ref: RDW-2025)

Hi all —

Per Rishi’s note, attached is Redwood’s proposed redline for Section 7 and a one‑page summary ("OrderForm-Liability-Summary.xlsx") that maps the carve-outs to examples. High-level positions:

- Cap: standard 1x fees in the Order Form remains the general cap.
- Fraud / willful misconduct: carve-out remains uncapped for proven fraud or intentional wrongdoing.
- Gross negligence: propose a limited exception where liability may exceed the cap only if the claimant proves (i) a material breach of the MSA and (ii) reckless disregard for the contractual obligations (both elements required). This protects against broad negligence claims tied to product defects.
- Consequential damages: keep exclusion, but expressly carve back for third‑party claims arising from unauthorized access to regulated customer data where Redwood’s grossly negligent or willful misconduct caused the breach.

Draft sample clause (for redline):
"Notwithstanding the foregoing, neither party’s aggregate liability under this Order Form shall exceed the total fees paid by Customer to Redwood under the applicable Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim, except that this limitation shall not apply (a) to damages arising from proven fraud or willful misconduct, or (b) to damages proven to have resulted from a material breach of this Agreement by Redwood in connection with reckless conduct or deliberate disregard of its contractual obligations."

Please review; we aimed for narrow tests to preserve the cap while addressing ACME’s regulator-related concerns. I also flagged the SLA exceptions in the redline where we can add additional remedies (service credits) instead of monetary exposure.

Attachment: ACME_MSA_redline_v3.docx

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

From: Julia Ramos <julia.ramos@acme.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form liability language (MSA ref: RDW-2025)

Laura — thanks for the draft and the clear summary. A few quick points from Acme Legal: 

1) We appreciate the two‑element test for gross negligence, but we are worried that requiring "material breach" + "reckless conduct" is too high a bar to make victims whole in cases where the harm is real but proving materiality is difficult. Can we consider "gross negligence demonstrated by a failing to follow Redwood’s documented security procedures resulting in unauthorized access" as an alternative path?

2) For fraud and willful misconduct, we need explicit carveouts for regulatory fines and penalties that are imposed on Acme as a result of Redwood’s willful misconduct.

3) Service credits are helpful but we may still need monetary remedy in a narrow set of data breach outcomes.

We’ll redline the document and send back suggested language next. For timing, we’re aiming to finalize before Acme’s procurement cut-off on 26 Sep.

Best,
Julia

From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: Julia Ramos <julia.ramos@acme.com>, laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order Form liability language (MSA ref: RDW-2025)

Julia — thanks for the feedback. Two suggested edits that balance Acme’s concern and Redwood’s need to limit open exposure: 

1) Add an alternative gross negligence pathway: retain the material breach + reckless standard as the primary test but add a second, narrower path where liability may exceed the cap if Acme proves (a) Redwood failed to follow Redwood’s published security procedures specifically applicable to Customer’s deployment, and (b) such failure caused unauthorized access to regulated data resulting in third‑party regulatory fines or penalties. This keeps the standard high but avoids the full "open-ended negligence" route.

2) Explicitly state that regulatory fines and penalties imposed on Customer as a direct result of Redwood’s proven willful misconduct or the narrow security-failure path are recoverable notwithstanding the limitation of liability.

Proposed sentence to insert after the gross‑negligence carve‑out: 
"For the avoidance of doubt, proof that (i) Redwood materially failed to adhere to its published security procedures applicable to Customer’s deployment, and (ii) such failure directly resulted in unauthorized access to Customer’s regulated data and in third‑party regulatory fines or penalties, shall be deemed a material breach supporting recovery notwithstanding the liability cap."

If that’s acceptable, we’ll update the redline and provide a tracked version for Acme to review.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Contracts Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Julia Ramos <julia.ramos@acme.com>
To: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Order Form liability language (MSA ref: RDW-2025)

Team — this compromise looks workable to Acme. We will incorporate the two‑path gross negligence language and the explicit carveback for regulatory fines into our redline and send the DocuSign-ready Order Form. One request: please confirm that the security procedures referenced are the public pages (https://docs.redwood.com/security) and any deployment‑specific runbooks Redwood provided during onboarding. If you can confirm by COB Monday we’ll proceed to signature.

Attachment: ACME_proposed_redline.docx

Thanks,
Julia Ramos
